title: Face with Steam From Nose Emoji 😤: Angry or Triumphant?
description: 😤 looks furious, but it was designed as a look of triumph. Learn how the steam-from-nose emoji means frustration, pride or gym-level determination today.
summary: The 😤 face with steam from nose huffs two puffs of air with closed eyes and a frown. Western users mostly read it as fuming with frustration or indignation. It was originally meant to show triumph and pride, and it is still widely used for determination, as in “let's go” before a challenge.
meaning: Two meanings live in this emoji, and they pull in opposite directions. The first is irritation: someone huffing after being disrespected, ignored or made to wait. “He left me on read 😤” is annoyed, a little haughty, and not yet truly angry. The emoji suits indignation better than rage, the mood of crossed arms and a sharp exhale.

The second meaning is the original one. Unicode once named this character “face with look of triumph,” reflecting a Japanese comics convention in which a forceful snort through the nose shows pride, defiance or fighting spirit. A character who has just won, or who refuses to back down, exhales exactly like this. Seen that way, the closed eyes are smug, not pained.

Modern usage blends the two into determination. Athletes and gym-goers post 😤 to mean locked in and ready to work, fans use it when their team is fired up, and people celebrating a hard-earned success add it as a proud “and I did that.” Because readers may see anger where the sender meant confidence, the words around it matter more than usual.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: As a complaint, it expresses being put out: bad service, a rude comment, a partner who forgot to take out the trash. It is often half playful, a show of being offended. After good news, as in “passed on the first try 😤,” it switches to pride, like blowing on your knuckles.

contexts.label: In sports and fitness
contexts.body: This is its most confident setting. Captions such as “5am workout done 😤” or “playoffs start tonight 😤” signal intensity and readiness. Paired with 💪 or 🔥 it is pure motivation. Opposing fans may use the same emoji to stew over a referee's call, so both senses show up on game day.

contexts.label: From a crush or partner
contexts.body: Here it is usually mock annoyance. “You didn't say goodnight 😤” is a pout that invites you to make it up to them, not a real accusation. If the surrounding messages are short and cold, take the frustration more seriously.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It can read as hostile in a professional chat, because colleagues will assume the angry meaning. Use it only with teammates who know your style, for example to celebrate shipping a difficult project, and never in reply to a request.

examples.text: Waited 40 minutes and they gave my table away 😤

examples.meaning: Proud and pumped after an achievement.

examples.text: You watched the finale without me?? 😤
examples.meaning: Playfully offended at a friend or partner.

examples.text: Nobody believed we could win. Look at us now 😤

examples.meaning: Focused and ready to take on a challenge.

combos.meaning: Determined and strong; standard gym and motivation pairing.
Fired up and ready to compete.
Irritated and unimpressed with someone's behavior.
Proud applause, often for one's own team or effort.

confusedWith.difference: 😠 scowls with open, glaring eyes and is plainly angry. 😤 closes its eyes and snorts, which reads as huffy, proud or determined. Only 😤 can be positive.
😮‍💨 blows a single puff from its mouth in a sigh of relief, tiredness or disappointment. 😤 blows two jets from its nose with a frown, showing frustration or resolve.
😡 is bright red and furious. 😤 stays yellow and is far milder: annoyed, indignant or simply fired up.

avoid: Do not use it with people who may take it as real anger, especially at work.
Avoid replying with it alone to someone's apology, since it looks like you are still fuming.
If you mean pride or motivation, add words or 💪 so the reader does not see a tantrum.
design: A yellow face with closed eyes, slanted eyebrows, a frown and two white puffs of steam shooting from the nostrils. All major platforms keep these elements. Some draw the brows angrily, pushing the design toward fury, while others look more smug, which is closer to the original idea of a victorious snort.

faqs.a: It can be either. Most English speakers use it for frustration or indignation, but its original Unicode name was “face with look of triumph,” and it is still common for pride and determination. Check the message it comes with.

faqs.q: What does 😤 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Often that he is fired up or proud, particularly around sports, the gym or a win. In a conversation between the two of you, it is usually playful annoyance, such as pretending to be offended that you ignored him.

faqs.q: What does 😤 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: Typically mock frustration or a pout: she is letting you know something bothered her without making it a fight. It can also mean she is feeling determined or pleased with herself after an accomplishment.

faqs.q: Why does the triumph emoji have steam coming out of its nose?
faqs.a: In Japanese manga and anime, a sharp snort through the nose shows a character full of pride, energy or defiance. The emoji came from that tradition. Outside Japan the same image suggests an angry bull, hence the mixed meanings.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 😤 and 😮‍💨?
faqs.a: 😮‍💨 is a sigh: relief, fatigue or resignation. 😤 is a huff: irritation, pride or determination. One lets tension go, the other builds it up.
